body:
Good Sunday morning, Bakersfield. The story leading the day is the return of the Latination art exhibit to downtown, where the Arts Council of Kern filled N Street with vendors, dancers, and more than a hundred pieces of local art celebrating the county's Latino community. Outside, expect a high near 78 under clear skies, with moderate air quality and no active weather alerts or fires anywhere in Kern County.

## The Kern Overnight

Gunfire calls carried through the small hours. At 3:37 a.m., officers were sent to a large party after a caller said his father had been shot and reported a victim down in a backyard. Multiple callers told dispatchers they had heard gunshots. Officers arrived and found no one in the yard.

About half an hour earlier, at 3:01 a.m., callers counted roughly five gunshots in the 1800 block of Hendricks Lane in south Bakersfield. A four-door car was seen driving away afterward, and a witness reported that four or five people got out of it and went into a home at the end of the cul-de-sac.

The hours around those calls were busy with weapons reports. At 7 p.m., a caller told deputies his mother was armed with a firearm and he believed she was preparing to use it while a 2-year-old and a 4-year-old were with her; she refused to come down. At 8:16 p.m., officers were sent to a home where a man had barricaded himself in a back room with two juveniles and would not come out — he had said his 12-year-old daughter let someone into the house. At 8:25 p.m., a man doing donuts in a Mustang was reported to have a firearm in his waistband. A fight in the 5500 block of College Avenue in east Bakersfield at 9:12 p.m. brought reports that adults had supplied juveniles with alcohol and that a man had a knife. At 9:30 p.m., a woman with a knife jumped a fence onto church property on North Chester Avenue. At 12:27 a.m., someone locked themselves in a restroom at a hospital emergency room lobby and appeared to be in a mental health crisis.

The night's most serious medical call came earlier. A crash at a park at 8:41 p.m. left at least four people hurt, two of them tagged black, and pinned a child's legs under the front of a vehicle. Crews called three units to the scene.

## Today's weather

It's 54 degrees at Meadows Field this morning, on the way to a high near 78 and a low around 55 tonight. No active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County, and no active fires are being reported. Air quality sits at 80 on the index — moderate — so most people can be outside without trouble, though those who are sensitive to particulates may want to keep an eye on it as the day warms. It's a good Sunday to be out and about.

## Top stories

**The Arts Council of Kern brought its annual Latination exhibit back to downtown Bakersfield over the weekend, and 23ABC reports organizers saw more participating artists than last year.** N Street between 19th and 18th streets was closed off and filled with vendors and dance performances, though the footprint was smaller than last year because of road construction. Arts Council director Jeanette Richardson told the station the event raised about $37,000 in its first year and that this year's show includes 107 art pieces, not counting kids' work. Founder Don Martin said he created Latination to honor what the Latino community has brought culturally to Kern County, asking artists for their own interpretations. Proceeds go back into the council's programs, which reach prisons and school districts across the county.

**In Delano, residents of the small community of Pond are pouring concrete and bracing for heavy rain three years after floodwaters pushed them out of their homes, according to 23ABC.** Residents say they're preparing without help from local, county, or state government. Store owner Bilqees Ubadi is pouring concrete around her business to keep water out after the 2023 flood got inside; she told the station she was displaced for about a year. Longtime resident Carmen Del Rio said she stayed with her son in Wasco for more than a month while they drained and cleaned her house, and that her landlord still hasn't cleaned up the damage. Residents said they asked officials for help preparing this time and were told Poso Creek, whose contaminated water overflowed and flooded Pond, is unincorporated.

**Cal State Bakersfield's College of Business and Public Administration has grown enrollment nearly 25% over the past three years, 23ABC reports, and college leaders say it wasn't an accident.** Dean Dr. Deborah Cours said faculty and staff deliberately increased outreach to local high schools, community colleges, chambers of commerce, and professional groups like the Kern County Society for Human Resource Management. The college has also aimed its programs at industries tied to the local economy — entrepreneurship, accounting, health care management, public administration, and a growing supply chain and logistics program. The agricultural business program has grown since it launched a decade ago, and the MBA and Master of Public Administration programs remain healthy. Cours pointed to employer partnerships with Target Distribution Center, Valley Strong, PepsiCo, Frito-Lay, Grimmway, and Bolthouse Fresh Foods as ways students get real-world experience.

**KGET 17 reports that a new Angel Walk is bringing hope to domestic violence survivors in Bakersfield.** The station also has coverage of Week 10 of the high school football season around Bakersfield and Kern County, and reports that Bakersfield police are searching for a suspect in an east Bakersfield burglary. Bakersfield Now, meanwhile, reports that rain is bringing a change to Kern County as winter approaches.

## Something good

The Latination exhibit is more than a weekend of vendors and dance performances. It's a reminder that the Arts Council of Kern takes the arts to people rather than waiting for them to come downtown — into prisons, into school districts around the county, into neighborhoods that don't always get a gallery on their block. More artists joined this year than last, and every dollar raised goes back into that work.

## Coming up this week

The Fox Theater has a full slate ahead. REZA | Edge of Illusion takes the stage today, October 25. Ghost Tours with J & J Investigations run Monday, October 26 and Tuesday, October 27 — two chances to hear the theater's own stories after dark. Elias Medina performs Friday, October 30, and Journey USA brings the tribute show to the Fox on Saturday, November 7. Looking further out, the Cults & Classics Season Pass for 2026–2027 is on sale for a run that begins August 24.

No public meetings are on the calendar for this week as of this morning. If you're heading to any of the Fox shows, give yourself a few extra minutes for downtown parking, and keep an eye on the forecast — Bakersfield Now notes rain is on the way as winter approaches, which matters most right now to the folks in Pond who are pouring concrete while the ground is still dry.

top.title: Latination art exhibit returns to downtown Bakersfield, celebrating Kern County's Latino community
